title: Tested: 2027 Mercedes-Maybach S680 V-12 Delivers Old-World Opulence - Road & Track
content: Nobody needs a V-12. But the top Maybach version of the S-Class makes an excellent case for still wanting one. No matter the form, Maybach’s take on the Mercedes S-Class is not for the sort of person worried about the optics of arriving in style. For the past decade, Maybach has been turned into a theater of opulence. Over the top is the whole point, with the Maybach logo as prominent on some cars as the Louis Vuitton emblem on hugely expensive bags. So it makes sense that Maybach goes one step further. The V-8-powered Maybach S580 is there if you want it, and any rational person probably should, but the ultraluxury-sedan buyer is rarely rational. For those who demand the most Maybach version of a Maybach sedan, the S680 still packs 12 cylinders of silky-smooth urge under its elegant hood. Our expert editors test every vehicle we review. Read more about how we test and review cars here. The 2027 Mercedes-Maybach S680 is, as its name implies, positioned about 100 points of badge better than the S580. The key distinction here is a twin-turbocharged V-12 that can trace its origins back over 20 years. The rest will look familiar, from the traditional three-pointed star hanging atop the massive front grille to the light-up Maybach wordmark below it. V-12 aside, the centerpiece is still the air suspension, Airmatic in Mercedes-Benz parlance, that is in this application aided by tech that scans the road to adjust the system for whatever it faces next. Despite having 50 percent more capacity and cylinders than the V-8 S580, the range topper’s power output is not correspondingly higher. The S680 makes relaxed peaks of 621 hp and 664 lb-ft, those figures being 91 hp and 111 lb-ft higher than the corresponding ones for the smaller-engine car. Mercedes claims identical 4.3-second 0–60-mph times for both cars. But numbers will only ever be a small part of the story for cars like this. Transmission: Nine-speed automatic, all-wheel drive EPA Fuel Economy: 12 mpg city, 20 mpg highway, 14 mpg combined Many modern Mercedes products, AMG badged ones in particular, are harsh and explosive things. For the past decade, the company’s performance badge has been building all shapes and sizes of car that explode off the line with turbocharged power and stay flat under heavy cornering loads. The Maybach S680 does none of that. The twin-turbocharged V-12 produces a superabundance of torque, but the 664 lb-ft delivers an effortlessness that makes it easy to experience acceleration that is both impressive and relaxing at the same time—satisfying an owner-driver behind the wheel but not disturbing them if they experienced the same forces while luxuriating in the back. Braking, too, mostly comes in the form of champagne stops, bringing the car to a rest without spilling a drop of a passenger’s drink. The S680 can stop itself in a hurry if it needs to, but the normal slowdown won’t disturb a sleeping occupant. In a world where powerful cars fight hard to defeat body roll and the once-sluggish response of automatic transmissions, the S680 is a throwback. It experiences noticeable lean under cornering loads, and it never feels responsive even in its sharpest Sport drive mode. The gearbox also decides to shift to its own agenda, rather than where a driver might expect it to. Rolls-Royce used to describe this sort of stately performance as “adequate,” and while the Maybach is capable of lifting its skirts in a way that old Rollers never could, the descriptor is still perfect for the way it delivers without ever seeming to break a sweat. Sure, it felt a little out of place on a quick run up and down the famous Angeles Crest Highway, a road with as many corners as straights. But any buyer looking for an S-Class to excel in that situation would most likely opt for the S63 AMG version. The Maybach is nobody’s one-car performance solution; it’s an ultraluxurious product designed to waft along the road in style. Materials are spectacular, particularly at this price point, which is well below what you’d pay for a similarly optioned Bentley or Rolls-Royce product. This is nobody’s idea of a subtle car, but those worried about the perceived stealthy nature of an ultraluxury sedan based on a mere luxury sedan can make their S680 stand out with a wide array of options from Mercedes’s Manufaktur range. That list includes more than 50 unique colors or combinations, plus a couple of dozen leather finishes. Buyers looking for something even more exclusive can head to the new Made to Measure studio in Los Angeles to spec a car from hundreds of individual options. The red interior optioned on the car I tested was certainly striking. Plenty of the two-tone options that have become a hallmark of Maybach offerings are available, including this far-from-subtle black and dark gray metallic pairing that could arguably stand to be a little bit more ostentatious. The key option is a $6000 Executive Rear Seat package. This drops the middle seat and all the compromises that come with it, leaving room for an $1100 refrigerated rear center console and a $3200 set of silver-plated champagne flutes. Those options might not exactly be a must, but the reclining right-rear seat is a particularly special place made all the more spectacular by the car’s impressive Burmester sound system. Buyers choosing the S680 for the noises its turbocharged V-12 produces may be disappointed to learn that excellent sound dampening kept things quiet throughout the cabin. This is a good thing, though; more than anything else, that peace and control over the environment inside the car is what makes an ultraluxury car feel special. The hallmark of the V-8 car, the Mercedes-Maybach S580, is that it is the standout bargain in the ultraluxury-sedan segment. The extra sum of cash to buy the V-12 moves the S680 back toward the range of the Bentley Flying Spur, an all-time great car that is significantly better at the performance tasks the Maybach intentionally ignores. Still, this car starts at a lower number and should typically come out to be less expensive after being optioned to a similar level. Plus it has a V-12, whereas the Spur has a hybridized V-8. The Rolls-Royce Ghost has 12 cylinders, but it also costs over $100,000 more. The S680 comes with the key advantage of sitting at the very top of the Maybach pecking order. This is the car people think of when they say the name, the closest thing to a successor to the 57 and 62 sedans that relaunched the brand for 2003. Wearing the two-tone paint that best shows off the massively extended rear doors that come with the 7.1-inch wheelbase stretch over the standard S-Class, the Maybach S680 manages to look the proverbial million dollars at what’s nearly a 75 percent discount. For the buyers Mercedes is targeting, the massive presence is a huge selling point. That leaves one major question: Why opt for the V-12 over the V-8? The extra torque certainly helps move the hefty sedan in effortless comfort, sure, but the real answer might be even more simple—for some, bigger will always be better. As happy as we are to see the V-12 live for another generation, the S680’s advantages over the S580 are more emotional than rational. But if you’re going to buy a Maybach, wouldn’t you want it to be the best one? Lounge-style rear seating is a must for anyone optioning out a car like this, and the Maybach team has a strong understanding of how to make that space feel special. With the seat fully reclined, massage functions active, and chilled champagne in those ridiculous logo-adorned silver flutes, a properly equipped S680 is rolling serenity. title: Before the Sensor: Filter Ordering and Self-Collision in Amsted Rail v. Squires - Patently-O
content:
The Federal Circuit has affirmed the cancellation of claims in Amsted Rail's railcar monitoring patent, along with the Board's refusal to let Amsted swap in substitute claims. Amsted Rail Co. v. Squires, No. 2025-1063 (Fed. Cir. July 24, 2026) (nonprecedential). U.S. Patent No. 10,137,915 covers sensor nodes and radios bolted onto freight cars to watch for derailments, damaged wheels, and overheating bearings. Claim 1 recites: ... (b) one or more sensors ... configured to measure accelerations of the railcar; and
(c) one or more filters configured to filter at least a portion of the accelerations ... Amsted argued the two elements as a sequence: measure first, filter second. But the panel held that the claim imposes no order, which opened the door to invalidating prior art. Both appeals were argued on June 1: this one and a companion covering two more Amsted patents, which the same panel disposed of on June 3 with a one word Rule 36 judgment. Ordering. A claim does not require its elements to operate in sequence unless the language, as a matter of logic or grammar, demands it, or unless the specification makes the sequence part of the invention. Amsted's hook was the definite article: claim 1's filters filter "the accelerations," which Amsted said refers back to the accelerations measured by the sensors. But the Board read "the accelerations" as including physical motion of the railcar rather than the signal alone, and the panel agreed. On that reading a silicone pad that keeps unwanted frequencies from ever reaching the accelerometer is filtering accelerations in the sense claim 1 uses. title: Kim leads ‘V-Day’ events as North Korea highlights Chinese help in Korean War - NK News
content:
North Korean leader Kim Jong Un attended events Monday marking the 73rd anniversary of the “victory in the Fatherland Liberation War” over the U.S., according to state media, emphasizing China’s assistance in the war. The Korean Central News Agency (KCNA) reported Tuesday that the July 27 concert took place at the Pyongyang Indoor Stadium, followed by a small-scale military parade outside the venue to celebrate the so-called victory in the 1950-53 Korean War. The concert included a video segment showing Kim and Chinese leader Xi Jinping’s recent meeting in Pyongyangand clips of Chinese troops during the war. Chinese Ambassador North Korean leader Kim Jong Un attended events Monday marking the 73rd anniversary of the “victory in the Fatherland Liberation War” over the U.S., according to state media, emphasizing China’s assistance in the war. The Korean Central News Agency (KCNA) reported Tuesday that the July 27 concert took place at the Pyongyang Indoor Stadium, followed by a small-scale military parade outside the venue to celebrate the so-called victory in the 1950-53 Korean War. The concert included a video segment showing Kim and Chinese leader Xi Jinping’s recent meeting in Pyongyang and clips of Chinese troops during the war. Chinese Ambassador to the DPRK Wang Yajun and Russian Chargé d’Affaires Vladimir Topekha were invited as special guests. KCNA said attendees were “deeply touched” by the “matchless self-sacrificing spirit, heroism and brilliant feats of excellent sons and daughters of the Chinese people who shared life and death” and fought “shoulder to shoulder” with North Koreans in the war. China entered the Korean War in Oct. 1950, pushing U.S.-led forces back from their advance toward the Chinese border and ultimately stabilizing the front near the 38th parallel. North Korean founding leader Kim Il Sung invaded the South four months earlier in an attempt to unify the peninsula under his rule. Major hostilities were halted on July 27, 1953, with the signing of the Armistice Agreement by the DPRK, China and the U.S.-led U.N. Command. North Korean propaganda continues to call the July 27 holiday the “Day of Victory” while falsely claiming it was a righteous war to repel an invasion by South Korea and the U.S. Monday’s performances were meant as a message of the “DPRK people’s eternal thanks to the brave fighters of the Chinese People’s Volunteers,” KCNA reported, calling the war a joint mission of “resisting America.” “The DPRK-China friendship, based on the shared ideal and militant fraternity, will be immortal along with the history of the great war victory,” it added. Kim also visited the Cemetery of the Fallen Soldiers of the Chinese People’s Volunteers (CPV) on Sunday to pay his respects to Chinese soldiers. He visited the cemetery in October and around the July 27 holiday in 2023 as well, when state media presented a similarly high emphasis on Chinese assistance to mark the 70th anniversary. The focus on China was more subdued at anniversary events in the last two years, but Beijing and Pyongyang have recently appeared to seek closer relations again after the DPRK’s pandemic-era policies slowed down business ties and ended Chinese tourism. State media characterized the celebratory events as an “ideological and mental nutrient” for the North Korean people and military, encouraging patriotism and loyalty to the state. Kim attended the concert with his wife Ri Sol Ju and his young daughter. State TV cameras focused closely on the leader and his daughter during its coverage, as has become standard in recent years, but the KCNA text report did not mention his family’s presence. They didn’t appear at the parade with Kim, who appeared on the viewing platform with current and retired generals, as well as elderly war veterans who should now be in their late 80s and 90s. Kim did not make a speech at this year’s events after doing so at July 27 celebrations in years past. Defense minister No Kwang Chol delivered brief remarks at what KCNA called the “ceremonial parade of the columns symbolic of the units who fought in the Fatherland Liberation War.” He vowed to remain vigilant against “forces that are threatening at every moment,” but did not  include pointed messages at the U.S. and ROK. The parade featured around a dozen block formations, each with 160 young soldiers wearing Korean War-era uniforms and representing divisions named after famous generals and celebrated battles like the “liberation” of Seoul. KCNA praised soldiers who became “human bombs” in the war by carrying out suicide attacks, echoing North Korea’s active policy in the Ukraine war requiring soldiers to kill themselves to complete attacks and avoid capture. Symbolic units of horse-drawn carriages and motorcycles rounded out the historical procession, followed by three formations representing the current-era army, navy and air force to end the parade. Similar concerts and military marches took place at the Pyongyang Indoor Stadium on July 27 in 2024 and 2025 as well, with Kim skipping last year’s events. While North Korea is still engaged in a war alongside Russia against Ukraine, the holiday does not generally serve as a memorial day for all war casualties and Monday’s events appeared mostly focused on the Korean War. title: Storylines | Royals v. Spirit: A Home Test Against the League Leaders - Real Salt Lake
content: All eyes will be on America First Field this Wednesday, July 29 as Utah Royals FC welcome star forward Trinity Rodman and the Washington Spirit to the Wasatch Front. The midweek matchup will mark the Royals second of three matches played in a congested nine day period. Following the exciting 4-1 victory over the weekend, the home side will look to continue its dominance in front of the home crowd. This edition of storylines will dive into how the Royals have continued to break records in its strongest season in club history, the squad's impressive ability to work as a unit and URFC’s history with the dominant Washington side. Since dropping two matches in its return to NWSL play following the 2026 FIFA World Cup, URFC has bounced-back, winning two consecutive matches to regain the strong form showcased during the first half of the season. While the Royals may not have what is considered as one “big-name” player like opposing squads, the home side has pointed out the importance of every single player on its roster who have worked tirelessly and as one to boost the Royals in its record breaking season towards the top of the NWSL standings. While the Royals have key attacking pieces on its roster like, Canadian forward Cloé Lacasse and Japanese star Mina Tanaka, the squad boasts an impressive nine different goal scorers thus far in 2026, making URFC a difficult team to plan against as any one player from any position can break through to find the back of the net. Utah’s road match against the North Carolina Courage last Saturday, July 25th was the perfect example of this, with four set-piece goals (including penalties) scored by four different players across three different positions. Captain Kate Del Fava opened up the scoring with fellow defender Tatumn Milazzo netting the game winning goal just 18 minutes later, bringing both center backs onto the score sheet in the same match for the first time. While Del Fava earned her first goal in over two years, Milazzo now has a career high three goals in a season. Along with the defenders showcasing brilliance on both ends of the pitch was Tanaka who netted her fifth goal of the season, bringing the Japanese international to an impressive ninth goal contribution of the season (5 goals, 4 assists) to tie Amy Rodriguez (2019) for third in club history. The midfielder continues to bring creativity and high-quality scoring abilities to the pitch, making her a threat to any opposition's defense. The Utah Royals offensive power cannot be explained without the impact of Lacasse, whose stoppage time penalty against the Courage helped to lift the Royals to its 4-1 victory and brought the forward to sole ownership of URFC’s 2026 Golden Boot race with six goals and four assists. The veteran brings a speed and fierce presence to the pitch that not only lifts herself but the whole team in earning results. Lacasse’s 10 goal contributions this season have now brought her equal with the Utah Royals single-season club record set by Christen Press in 2019, with 14 matches left in 2026, the Canadian has ample time to write herself further into Utah’s history books. While the Royals attack has been explosive this season, the work of its backline led by goalkeeper Mandy McGlynn has been key in keeping the squad in matches. With five massive saves on Saturday, McGlynn has continued to showcase her high level ability to read the game and remains a force between the posts with 24 saves and four clean sheets on the season. The veteran keeper will need to continue to work seamlessly with her backline in order to earn a result against the explosive attack of Washington on Wednesday. As the Royals gear up to take on league-leading Washington Spirit on Wednesday night, it is imperative to look back at the squad's history with the visiting side since its return to Utah in 2024. While the Royals overall record of 1-2-2 (W-L-T) against the Spirit looks to favor the visitors, URFC has remained unbeaten in three straight meetings with Washington, taking one victory and two draws. Most recently, the Royals traveled to Audi Field on March 25, 2026 earning a 1-1 draw. While URFC fell behind in the 18th minute, the visitors refused to quit, continuing to pressure on and off the ball in search of a goal. With a belief that never wavered, Tanaka, fresh off an AFC Asian Cup win, netted the equalizer in the 84th minute to help the squad earn a point in what many consider to be one of the most difficult road environments in the NWSL; Washington's home stadium. The Spirit have continued to be a force in the league, with many goal scoring threats on its roster like Italian forward Sofia Cantore who has four goals and one assist on the season. One main attacking threat the Royals will face on Wednesday is USWNT standout, Trinity Rodman. The 24-year-old forward is a force in the offensive third, having used her speed and impressive footwork to net seven goals and five assists thus far in 2026. URFC’s backline will need to work cohesively to thwart any attacks by Rodman in order to keep her off the scoresheet. While the visitors have the attacking power of Rodman, URFC has proven itself as a squad that can exploit opposing defenses and go toe-to-toe with any squad in the NWSL. The key for the Royals in a game where it will undoubtedly see immense pressure, is to get on the scoresheet first. While the home side boasts an impressive 9-2-0 (W-T-L) record when doing so, Washington has yet to lose a match when scoring first earning a 10-0-1 record. Drawing first blood will be an important momentum boost for the home side in its hopes for a victory on Wednesday. The midweek home matchup against the first-place Washington Spirit is scheduled to kickoff at 7 PM MT with tickets still available for purchase. Following Wednesday’s match, URFC remain at America First Field for a second consecutive match, welcoming Sophia Wilson and the Portland Thorns on Sunday, August 2nd. Kickoff is scheduled for 5 PM MT with tickets for both matches are available for purchase here. URFC takes on Washington Spirit at home.
